chapter: New Orleans bands, brass bands and learning bass
title: The potato man and a brick thrown on Canal Street
summary: Fake-playing musicians, then Garland's story of borrowing a trombone for a parade, having no lip and being hit by a brick at Exchange Alley.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Them days passing. Yeah, he used to take guys out, we go to play a job and he said we'd be shot on the mountain. We'd have a guy with a guitar and he used to be sitting up there and we'd be doing nothing like motioning. Yeah. You know, people got wise to that. You know what a potato man is?
Did you ever hear of a potato man?
You'd have to take a potato and stuff it down the horn and make sure he doesn't play anything. Did you ever hear of that?
Ah, that's okay. Come on in if you want to.
Well I know I was coming up.
Okay, you coming up Canal Street? I was coming up Canal Street, was playing a parade and I couldn't get no mellophone.
I was playing an alto, you know, upright alto.

Yeah. The mellophone is round like a, what you call them horns. That's what you call them. We'd call them peck horns, you know. And the Jews have rented all the horns out. I got to have me a horn. I looked up and they see the trombone. I said, give me the trombone. I got the trombone. I said, I'll play peck horn on the trombone. I'll play peck horn on the trombone. I was coming to Canal Street, I was being worried. There's a front, you know. I was, I hit the lick. Ain't nothing come out there.
So we got right to Canal and Exchange Alley.
You know where Exchange Alley is. It's still here. It's still here? Yeah. I asked about that, something about it. She said, you know nothing about it.

Yes sir. I got there, you know. White folk come right side me, you know. Put his ears to the hall, you know. I didn't know he had something down in his head, you know. Soon I got right there at that alley, whoop. He sure half a brick. He was trying to trouble. He run to the crowd.
He broke his lips, teeth and everything. He just threw it up in the hall, you know. Oh yeah. He'll knock it off, you know.

He's come home. The whole bastard, instead of playing, they laughing at me. I got out of the way to fight, man. He's trying to get that guy through that whole brick in the hall. I want to get all them. We had some awful times though.
